fixes.explanation: A new king, friend? Whoa, whoa, whoa. That's a whole different headline, and this psalm never prints it. What the many say is, "God will not deliver him." (Psalm 3:2). That's about whether God will rescue David, and nothing else. Don't let your brain bake in an extra ingredient the recipe never called for.

A river, friend? I can see it now: David standing there with enemies closing in, and the LORD is a nice, relaxing stream. Lovely for a picnic, not so much for a battle. David says, "But You, O LORD, are a shield around me…" (Psalm 3:3). A shield is what he reaches for, and it goes all the way around him.

True. David says the LORD is "…my glory, and the One who lifts my head." (Psalm 3:3). Verse 2 has many saying, "God will not deliver him," and verse 3 begins with "But You, O LORD…" I think a lifted head is a mighty fine thing to have when the crowd is that loud.

The king? Nope, not who David names. He says, "Salvation belongs to the LORD…" (Psalm 3:8). After a whole song about enemies, he doesn't hand the credit to anybody in a crown. He points straight to the LORD, and I think that's a humble way to end a song.
